summary: Dushanbe International Airport is the largest and busiest airport in Tajikistan, serving as the main gateway to the capital city of Dushanbe. The facility has undergone significant modernization in recent years, including a new terminal completed with international assistance. Set against the dramatic backdrop of the Tien Shan mountain foothills, it connects this Central Asian nation to destinations across Russia, China, the Middle East, and Europe.
faqs:
Q: How far is Dushanbe International Airport from the city center?
A: The airport is approximately 7-8 kilometers south of central Dushanbe, typically a 15-20 minute drive depending on traffic.

Q: Which airlines operate from Dushanbe Airport?
A: The airport serves as a hub for Somon Air and Tajik Air, with international carriers including Russian airlines, China Southern, flydubai, and Turkish Airlines operating regular flights.

Q: Is there a direct flight from Dushanbe to Moscow?
A: Yes, multiple daily flights connect Dushanbe to Moscow, operated by Somon Air, Tajik Air, S7 Airlines, and Ural Airlines.

Q: Does the airport have 24-hour operations?
A: The airport generally operates during scheduled flight hours, and passengers should confirm their flight times in advance as some facilities may close between late-night and early-morning departures.
transport_tips: Taxis are the most common way to reach the city center; arrange a ride through your hotel or use the official taxi services outside arrivals to avoid overcharging. Marshrutka (shared minibus) routes also serve the airport area and offer a budget-friendly option for travelers familiar with local transport. Ride-hailing apps may have limited availability, so planning transport in advance is recommended.
local_tip: Bring small denominations of local Tajik somoni or US dollars in cash—many shops and cafes in the terminal prefer cash, and having local currency on arrival helps with immediate expenses before reaching a bank or ATM in the city.
